system: SPT Masa PPN annexes — Formulir A1/A2 (output) and B1/B2/B3 (input); pre-Coretax numbering 1111 A2, 1111 B2, 1111 B3
frequency_detail: filed by the end of the month following the tax period (paling lambat akhir bulan berikutnya setelah masa pajak berakhir)
scope: all Pengusaha Kena Pajak (VAT-registered businesses); a reduced annex set applies to PKP using deemed input-tax guidelines, and a separate form (Induk + L1 + L2) applies to non-PKP VAT collectors
instrument: PER-44/PJ/2010 (Formulir 1111 and its Lampiran AB/A1/A2/B1/B2/B3); now PMK 81/2024 and PER-11/PJ/2025 Pasal 72(1) for the Coretax-era SPT Masa PPN
reasoning: The SPT Masa PPN is a master form (Induk) plus six annexes, and the annexes are not rate-band totals: the official completion instructions to PER-44/PJ/2010 give Formulir 1111 A2 the columns 'Nama Pembeli BKP / Penerima JKP', 'NPWP/Nomor Paspor', 'Faktur Pajak ... Kode dan Nomor Seri' and 'Tanggal', 'DPP', 'PPN', 'PPnBM', and the replaced/returned invoice serial — one row per tax invoice. Formulir 1111 B2 and B3 carry the mirror-image columns for the seller side. That is an invoice register travelling as a schedule to the return, so it is in scope on the content test even though it is an annex to the VAT return. The schedules survive Coretax: the SPT Masa PPN in Coretax still has an Induk plus A1, A2, B1, B2, B3 and C, and PER-11/PJ/2025 Pasal 72(1) re-enacts the same six annexes.
caveats: Note the mapping: B2 is the creditable domestic input tax list, B3 is non-creditable/facilitated input tax — the brief's '1111 B3 (input tax)' is the non-creditable list; the main purchase register is B2. What changed under Coretax (PMK 81/2024, live 1 Jan 2025) is administration, not content: A2 and B2 are now auto-posted from e-Faktur data the DJP already holds, so the taxpayer largely confirms rather than keys the register, but the filing itself is still an invoice-level list submitted by the taxpayer. Retail invoices issued 'digunggung' are reported in aggregate rather than per invoice. The 2011 start date of the 1111 annex structure could not be confirmed from a source that loaded, so the date given is the Coretax/PMK 81-2024 effective date; PER-44/PJ/2010 is the earlier instrument. Sources loaded: pajak.go.id/en/node/10244 (primary, confirms PER-44/PJ/2010 governs form 1111 and is still in force, but carries no annex detail); aguspajak.com mirror of the PER-44/PJ/2010 Lampiran II completion instructions (column headings); ortax.org on the Coretax form; news.ddtc.co.id on PER-11/PJ/2025 Pasal 72(1); online-pajak.com on Coretax A-2/B-2 detail. pajak.go.id/en/node/107920 loaded but was thin.

system: VAT declaration form 300.00 annexes — registers of invoices for acquired and for realised goods, works and services (historically 300.07 and 300.08)
frequency_detail: with form 300.00, due no later than the 15th of the second month following the reporting quarter
scope: VAT-registered persons filing form 300.00 — but in substance only those holding paper invoices (see caveats)
instrument: Order of the Minister of Finance No. 695 of 12 November 2025 approving the 2026 tax reporting forms (applies to relations arising from 1 January 2026); the paper-only rule rests on Tax Code art. 424(2)(2) as amended from 2018
reasoning: The registers still exist as annexes to form 300.00 and they are line-per-invoice — they set out details of individual invoices issued and received (counterparty identification, invoice number and date, turnover, VAT), not totals by rate. On the content test that is an invoice register filed as a schedule to the return, hence in scope. But the scope is now residual: since 2018, invoices issued or received in electronic form through the ESF system are not entered in the registers ('в реестрах 300.07 и 300.08 не отражаются счета-фактуры, выписанные или полученные в электронном виде'), by reference to Tax Code art. 424(2)(2), so a taxpayer whose invoicing is entirely electronic files no register at all. The transaction-level reporting in Kazakhstan has migrated into the ESF system itself, which is a continuous-transaction-control regime rather than a separate periodic filing.
caveats: Strong caveat for the country page: for most VAT payers this annex is now vestigial — ESF issuance is mandatory across almost all of the VAT base, and ESF invoices are excluded from the registers, so the schedule is filed only for residual paper invoices. If the site prefers a substance-over-form line, Kazakhstan is better described under clearance/CTC (ESF) than under e-reporting. Numbering: pro1c's 2026 form article, which loaded, lists annex 300.03 as removed for 2026 and shows the registers as 300.06 (realised) and 300.07 (acquired) with 300.08 as VAT refund information — i.e. the historic 300.07/300.08 numbering appears to have shifted for 2026. I could not verify that renumbering against the text of Order No. 695, so treat the 2026 annex numbers as unconfirmed. Sources: pro1c.kz line-by-line guide (loaded; quotes Tax Code art. 424(2)(2) and the paper-only rule); pro1c.kz 2026 form 300.00 page (loaded; Order No. 695 of 12 Nov 2025, effective 1 Jan 2026); pro1c.kz ESF/register article (loaded; 'since 2018 electronic invoices are not reflected in registers 300.07 and 300.08'); 1c-rating.kz (loaded; confirms 300.07/300.08 are line-per-invoice, but describes the 2012 form); mybuh.kz (loaded; deadline no later than the 15th of the second month). cdb.kz returned 404; 1cbit.kz returned 429 — both failed. No gazette or kgd.gov.kz text loaded.

system: Monthly Sales Tax and Federal Excise Return (STR-7) — Annexure-A (domestic purchases) and Annexure-C (domestic sales)
frequency_detail: Annexure-C by the 10th, payment by the 15th and the return by the 18th of the month following the tax period
scope: all sales-tax-registered persons (CNG-only taxpayers file quarterly)
instrument: Sales Tax Rules, 2006 — return form STR-7 prescribed under rule 14(1), with Annexure-A and Annexure-C
reasoning: The FBR return form itself shows Annexure-A and Annexure-C as one row per invoice, not totals by rate. Annexure-C (domestic sales) columns include buyer NTN/CNIC and name, document type and number, date of sale, sale type and rate, quantity and unit, value of sales excluding sales tax, sales tax/FED in ST mode, tax withheld at source, extra tax, and province of origination. Annexure-A (domestic purchases) mirrors this with supplier NTN/CNIC and name, document number, purchase date, value excluding sales tax, sales tax, withholding, input credit not allowed and HS code. That is a sales listing and a purchase listing filed as annexures to the return, so it is in scope on the content test; the STR-7 body is the summary declaration and would not be, on its own. Annexure-C is also filed on a separate, earlier deadline (the 10th) from the return itself (the 18th), which reinforces that it is a distinct transaction-level filing rather than part of the summary.
caveats: The FBR page confirming the 10th/15th/18th sequence loaded but does not describe the annexure columns; the form PDF that does carry the columns is the 2016-17 STRIVe version of STR-7, so column detail is from that vintage. No loaded source gave a commencement date for the invoice-wise annexures, so date is left null — the Sales Tax Rules, 2006 are the governing instrument but I could not confirm from a loaded source when the annexure format took its current shape. Separately, FBR's Digital Invoicing regime (real-time invoice transmission) has been rolling out and overlaps this obligation; that is a clearance-style channel and is not what this entry describes. Sources loaded: fbr.gov.pk 'File Sales Tax Return' page (primary; deadlines) and download1.fbr.gov.pk STR-7 form PDF (primary; annexure columns).

system: VAT return (Расчет НДС) annexes No. 4 and No. 5 — registers of invoices for acquired and for realised goods, works and services
frequency_detail: by the 20th of the month following the reporting month
scope: VAT-registered taxpayers filing the VAT return under the general regime
instrument: VAT return form approved by joint order of the Ministry of Finance and the State Tax Committee, registered with the Ministry of Justice as No. 3126 of 21 January 2019; new form version code 10006_45 applies from 1 January 2026; auto-preparation introduced by Law No. ZRU-1108 of 25 December 2025
reasoning: The VAT return carries five annexes, of which No. 4 is the 'Реестр счетов-фактур' for purchases and No. 5 the register for sales. These are filled per invoice: counterparty name and INN, invoice number and date, value excluding VAT, VAT amount and total including VAT, covering only transactions of the reporting month. That is a purchase listing and a sales listing filed as annexes to the return — in scope on the content test.
caveats: On the 2026 change: the amendment does exist but it does not abolish the register. Law No. ZRU-1108 of 25 December 2025 makes the tax authority prepare the VAT return (along with PIT, social tax and turnover tax) automatically rather than only on taxpayer request, and gives the taxpayer five business days to correct it. No source that loaded says the invoice register annexes were removed from the form, and the 2026 form (code 10006_45, effective 1 January 2026) is described as adding rows — including rows for VAT on high-risk e-invoices — not as dropping annexes. So the correct reading is that the taxpayer still files an invoice-level register, now pre-filled from ESF data, not that the register has gone. This should be re-checked against the text of the 2026 form before publication. The register column detail comes from a buxgalter.uz explainer written against the 2019 form. Sources loaded: buxgalter.uz VAT return completion guide (annexes 4 and 5, columns, MJ No. 3126 of 21.01.2019); buxgalter.uz on the 2026 form's new rows; ey.com Uzbekistan tax alert January 2026 (auto-preparation, Law No. ZRU-1108, five business days); moliyaviy.com reporting calendar (monthly, by the 20th). bss.uz returned 403 — failed. No soliq.uz or lex.uz page loaded.

level: invoice-level, but built by the tax authority
frequency: continuous (register), reconciled with the monthly Formulario 29
frequency_detail: the SII populates the register as DTEs arrive; any complementary entries must be made within the legal period for the monthly F29 declaration (F29 due monthly, generally by the 12th or the 20th for electronic filers)
scope: issuers and recipients of documentos tributarios electrónicos
instrument: Resolución Exenta SII N° 61 de 2017, which created the RCV and released taxpayers from keeping the Libro de Compras y Ventas and from sending the IECV
reasoning: This is the deciding question and it falls against inclusion. The SII's own FAQ states the register 'es abastecido por los documentos tributarios electrónicos (DTE's) que han sido recibidos por el Servicio de Impuestos Internos' — it is constructed by the SII from documents it already holds through the clearance channel, and it replaced both the Libro de Compras y Ventas and the IECV file that taxpayers used to send. There is no standing duty to transmit transaction data: the invoice data reaches the SII when the DTE is cleared, which is the excluded clearance step. The only residual taxpayer action is to inform documents held in non-electronic form (paper invoices, import declarations DIN, summaries of paper boletas) so the register is complete before the F29 — and a taxpayer operating exclusively with electronic documents has no complementary obligation at all. A gap-filling duty for documents outside the clearance channel is not the standing transmission duty the box is about.
caveats: Resolución Exenta N° 61 de 2017 itself did not load — sii.cl/documentos/resoluciones/2017/reso61.pdf was refused for provenance and searches on sii.cl surfaced reso86.pdf and reso13.pdf but not reso61. The substance is nonetheless confirmed from two SII pages that did load (the RCV FAQ PDF and the F29 'complementar información' page) plus a secondary summary. The FAQ gives the 1 August 2017 start and the replacement of the Libro; the secondary source attributes the resolution and notes taxpayers operating exclusively with electronic invoices have no complementary obligation. Sources loaded: sii.cl RCV FAQ PDF (primary), sii.cl F29 complementainfo page (primary), sienacloud.cl summary of Resolución 61 (secondary). transtecnia.cl returned 403 — failed.

system: VAT3 return in iTax — sales and purchase schedules (auto-populated VAT return)
frequency_detail: return and payment on or before the 20th day of the following month
instrument: VAT Act 2013 and the iTax VAT3 return; auto-population introduced by KRA from the March 2024 tax period, drawing on TIMS/eTIMS, non-resident digital service invoices and customs entries
reasoning: The VAT3 schedules are invoice-level, not rate-band totals: KRA's own FAQ describes the sales schedule as carrying, for each sale to a registered customer, the 'PIN of purchaser, invoice number, invoice date and taxable amount', and the purchase schedule as carrying PIN, invoice date, invoice number, customs entry number and taxable value. The taxpayer files these schedules as part of the return, so this is a sales listing and a purchase listing travelling with the return — in scope on the content test.
caveats: Since March 2024 the schedules arrive pre-populated from eTIMS/TIMS and customs, and the pre-populated lines cannot be altered (no editing of PIN, invoice number, invoice date, customs entry number, or upward adjustment of taxable value). The taxpayer's remaining input is a lump-sum field for sales and purchases not transmitted through eTIMS/TIMS. So the direction of travel is the same as Chile's — the authority already holds the data — but unlike Chile the taxpayer still files the invoice-level schedule as their return, rather than the authority maintaining a register. Before March 2024 the taxpayer compiled and uploaded the schedules themselves. Sources loaded: kra.go.ke VAT auto-populated return FAQ PDF (primary; schedule fields, data sources, March 2024) and kra.go.ke VAT publication PDF (primary; 20th-of-following-month deadline, iTax filing). gichuripartners.com loaded but was thin; kra.go.ke eTIMS FAQ page not fetched.

system: 세금계산서합계표 — aggregate tax invoice lists, filed as 매출처별 (by customer) and 매입처별 (by supplier) with the VAT return
frequency_detail: with the VAT return — final returns for the two six-month taxable periods by 25 January and 25 July, preliminary returns by 25 April and 25 October
scope: businesses that issued or received tax invoices
instrument: Value-Added Tax Act (부가가치세법) Article 54 (세금계산서합계표의 제출); form prescribed by the Enforcement Rules
reasoning: The 합계표 is per-counterparty, not invoice-level: it aggregates the invoices issued to (or received from) each trading partner and reports, per counterparty, the business registration number, trade name, number of invoices (매수), supply value (공급가액) and tax amount (세액), together with counts of counterparties and invoices. That is per-counterparty transaction data, which the stated principle puts in scope even though it is filed alongside the VAT return; it is not a return of totals by tax rate. Failure to submit, or omission, attracts a penalty of 0.5% of supply value (0.3% if late), which confirms it is a distinct filing obligation rather than a line of the return.
caveats: Important qualification: for electronic tax invoices whose issuance details were transmitted to the NTS by the 11th day of the month following the end of the taxable period, only a single aggregate figure is entered in the 'electronic tax invoice issued' box — no per-counterparty detail is required. Per-counterparty detail survives only for paper tax invoices and for electronic invoices transmitted from the 12th onward, which are combined and listed separately. So, as in Kazakhstan, the listing has been hollowed out by the e-invoicing channel. The stronger candidate for Korea's e-reporting box is arguably the separate duty to transmit 전자세금계산서 발급명세 to the NTS by the day after issuance — a transmission to the tax authority distinct from delivering the invoice to the buyer — rather than the 합계표. Sourcing is weak: law.go.kr and call.nts.go.kr both refused (robots.txt), so no primary text of VAT Act Article 54 or of the official form loaded. Sources loaded: taxguide.im (the 11th-of-the-following-month rule and the aggregate-only treatment), bolta.io (per-counterparty structure, fields, 0.5%/0.3% penalties), namu.wiki (매출처별/매입처별 preparation each taxable period), avalara.com (two six-month taxable periods plus preliminary quarterly returns, 25 days after period end). date left null — no loaded source states when the 합계표 obligation began.
